title: Gravecrawler + Phyrexian Altar + Carrion Feeder + Bastion of Remembrance: is the drain unbounded and does it cost anything?

you: Gravecrawler (2/1) — already sacrificed to pay the cost of the ability now on the stack

stack.object: Bastion of Remembrance's triggered ability — 'Whenever a creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life.' Triggered on Gravecrawler's death, which paid the cost of Phyrexian Altar's mana ability.

extras.pod_size: Five players — you and four opponents, 160 opposing life in total (opponent life is on the board block).
extras.library: You have 60 cards in your library.
assumptions: No player responds to anything; every opponent passes priority throughout.
No permanent enters or leaves the battlefield except as described by the cards named here.
It is your precombat main phase, so you have sorcery-speed permission when you hold priority with an empty stack.
Carrion Feeder is a Zombie and stays on the battlefield throughout — it is never the sacrifice.
Phyrexian Altar's ability is a mana ability, so it never used the stack and has already resolved; its mana is in your pool.
extras.note_for_the_resolver: This is the most-played combo line the deck contains (Commander Spellbook popularity 60,592) and it has never been resolved. Stack 009 on this deck is checker-passed and establishes the Gravecrawler graveyard-cast machinery — 113.6f, 604.6, 601.3 — for a board where the Zombie condition is met by Warren Soultrader. Here the Zombie is Carrion Feeder and the mana comes from Phyrexian Altar rather than a Treasure, so the sacrifice pays for the recast directly. Reuse that established chain; do not re-derive it at length.

scenario.question: Resolve the stack, then resolve one full further iteration. Can the loop be repeated an unbounded number of times from this board with no mana and no life from outside it, and what is the exact net change per completed iteration to your life total and to each opponent's life total?

steps.action: Establish what is on the stack, and check it against the corrected scenario. Phyrexian Altar's ability — 'Sacrifice a creature: Add one mana of any color.' — requires no target, could add mana when it resolves, and is not a loyalty ability, so it is a mana ability. A mana ability never uses the stack: it resolved immediately when it was activated and put {B} into your mana pool, where it stays as unspent mana until the end of the step or phase. Bastion of Remembrance's ability triggered on Gravecrawler's death, and that death happened DURING the payment of the Altar's activation cost — i.e. while an ability was being activated, which is expressly a time at which an ability may trigger. Nothing happened at that moment; the trigger was held and put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority.
steps.effect: The scenario now matches the rules and scenario-facts, so there is nothing to report as a disagreement: the stack holds exactly ONE object — Bastion of Remembrance's triggered ability at pos 0 — and {B} of your chosen colour (black, for Gravecrawler) is already in your mana pool with both Swamps tapped. Board entering the resolution: ONE creature body, Carrion Feeder; Phyrexian Altar and Bastion of Remembrance are the other permanents; Gravecrawler is listed only as the permanent already sacrificed to pay the cost and is in the graveyard, not on the battlefield. Four opponents at 40 each.

When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player’s mana pool. From there, it can be used to pay costs immediately, or it can stay in the player’s mana pool as unspent mana. Each player’s mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase

Each time a player would receive priority, each ability that has triggered but hasn’t yet been put on the stack is put on the stack.

steps.action: ANSWER — is the loop unbounded, and what does one iteration cost? Read the ledger off steps 5-10. Mana: {B} spent on the cast, {B} produced by the sacrifice — net 0, and no land ever untaps. Life paid: none (Phyrexian Altar's cost is a sacrifice only). Cards: none drawn, so the 60-card library is never touched. Bodies: Gravecrawler leaves the graveyard and returns to it; Carrion Feeder never moves and never gains a counter. Nothing in the iteration is consumed, so the set of actions can be repeated indefinitely and the shortcut rules apply.
steps.effect: YES, unbounded with no mana and no life from outside the board. Exact net change per completed iteration: YOUR life +1; EACH opponent -1 per seat, which is -4 across the four-seat pod — the per-seat and pod figures are not interchangeable and neither may be quoted as the other. Kill maths, per seat: each opponent starts at 40 and needs 40 drain events. The trigger already on the stack was event 1 (step 3), so 39 further iterations reduce all four opponents to 0 simultaneously; the state-based-action check after that 40th trigger resolves makes all four lose the game at once. You finish at 40 + 40 = 80 life. The Commander Spellbook line (popularity 60,592) is CONFIRMED as a true unbounded drain for this exact board.

final_state.summary: Phyrexian Altar's ability is a mana ability, so it never used the stack (605.3b) — it resolved on activation and put {B} in the mana pool. The corrected scenario says exactly that, so the stack holds ONE object: Bastion of Remembrance's trigger, which resolves for each opponent 40 -> 39 (pod 160 -> 156) and you 40 -> 41. One full further iteration then runs on nothing but this board: cast Gravecrawler from the graveyard for the {B} already in pool (permission from its own zone-modifying ability — 601.3 / 113.6f / 604.6 — with the Zombie condition met by Carrion Feeder, which the loop never sacrifices), let it resolve, sacrifice it to Phyrexian Altar for a fresh {B}, and let the single Bastion trigger resolve — each opponent 39 -> 38 (pod 156 -> 152), you 41 -> 42. The board returns to an identical state, so the loop is unbounded. Net per completed iteration: YOUR LIFE +1; EACH OPPONENT -1 per seat, -4 across the pod; mana 0; cards drawn 0; board unchanged; no life paid at any point. Per seat, 40 drain events are lethal; one has already resolved, so 39 further iterations put all four opponents at 0 at the same state-based-action check, and you end at 80 life. Bastion has TWO triggered abilities (an enters trigger making a 1/1 white Human Soldier token, and the death trigger); only the death trigger can fire in this loop, because Bastion never re-enters — so one trigger, one drain, per iteration. Bodies on your battlefield entering the resolution: one (Carrion Feeder) — Gravecrawler was spent paying the cost. Stack 009 shares this board's body count but not its composition (Warren Soultrader, not Carrion Feeder), so no figure is imported from it.

kill.all_four_opponents_reach_zero: simultaneously, at the state-based-action check after the 40th trigger resolves

Full text is about a state where a set of actions could be repeated indefinitely and the shortcut rules determining how many times. THE SWAP THE RESOLVER FLAGGED: JUDGED SOUND, NOT A SHORTCUT. 603.3 was dropped from steps 1 and 9 in favour of 117.2a. Compared the two full texts. 117.2a contains the whole put-on-the-stack sentence ('Each time a player would receive priority, each ability that has triggered but hasn't yet been put on the stack is put on the stack') AND the two propositions 603.3 lacks entirely: that a trigger may occur mid-activation, and that nothing happens when it does. What 603.3 uniquely carries is (a) 'The ability becomes the topmost object on the stack', (b) 'as an object that's not a card', (c) that it remains until countered or resolved, and (d) controller, which is actually 603.3a. NONE of that is load-bearing on this board: at step 1 and again at step 9 the stack is EMPTY when the trigger goes on it (step 8's mana ability never uses the stack), and both steps say only that Bastion's trigger is 'the only object on the stack' - a claim about count, not order. The contrast with 009 is the proof: 009 cited 603.3 at its steps 1 and 10 precisely BECAUSE ordering mattered there - its trigger had to go on the stack ABOVE Warren Soultrader's still-pending activated ability. 011 has no second stack object, so 603.3's unique sentence has nothing to do. The swap loses no support and adds the licence step 9 could not otherwise get. Keep it.

PREMISE-CONSISTENCY SWEEP OF THE WHOLE ARTIFACT, not just step 7 - passes. Searched every string field for trigger-count phrasing. Three places speak to it and all three now state the same premise: step 7 effect ('NOT because Bastion has only one trigger condition (it has two), but because neither of its two conditions matches a creature other than Bastion entering'), step 9 effect ('of Bastion's two triggered abilities only the death trigger can match here (its enters trigger needs Bastion itself to enter, and Bastion has not moved)'), and final_state.summary ('Bastion has TWO triggered abilities (an enters trigger making a 1/1 white Human Soldier token, and the death trigger); only the death trigger can fire in this loop, because Bastion never re-enters'). Nothing anywhere still asserts a single trigger condition. The absent Human Soldier token is also reconciled rather than ignored: step 7 notes the board as given and scenario-facts list Carrion Feeder as the only creature body, and the token's absence is legal - nothing requires a token made when Bastion entered, before this scenario begins, to still be there.

OMISSION CHECK ON A RULE 009 CITED AND 011 DOES NOT - correctly omitted. 009 had to dispose of summoning sickness at its step 9 because Gravecrawler is sacrificed the turn it enters.
